novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanistic relationship and measurement: “hallucinations coincide with weak subject enrichment at the recall locus” and therefore “Hallucination is the absence of retrieval, not corrupted retrieval.” Searches using “LLM hallucination weak factual retrieval subject enrichment,” “subject augmentation factual recall hallucination,” and “hidden-state knowledge absence hallucination detection” found the closest work to be Tracing and Dissecting How LLMs Recall Factual Knowledge for Real World Questions (ACL 2025), which already identifies a “Subject Augmentation and Broadcasting” phase, alongside established activation-based detectors such as INSIDE and ICR Probe. Relating the magnitude of that subject-stage signal specifically to retrieval absence—and distinguishing it from strong-but-wrong retrieval—is a non-trivial natural extension, but combining an existing recall-stage framework with established hidden-state hallucination detection is not a wholly new core paradigm.
